text:
laura: Hey team, customer jacob_cust reports SSO broken right after IdP cert rotation. They get a 403 from our ACS endpoint. Error from our logs: "SAML response recipient mismatch". They say login worked before cert rotate. Can someone look?

mika: Can you paste the SAMLResponse (base64) or decoded XML? Also which IdP and SP entityIDs were in use?

laura: Pasting redacted decoded assertion they sent (pulled from support ticket). Note: removed NameID.

laura: ```
<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol" ID="_a1b2c" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2026-04-15T12:34:56Z">
  <saml:Issuer xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">https://idp.customers.example.com/</saml:Issuer>
  <samlp:Status>
    <samlp:StatusCode Value="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Success"/>
  </samlp:Status>
  <saml:Assertion xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">
    <Issuer>https://idp.customers.example.com/</Issuer>
    <Subject>...
    </Subject>
    <AuthnStatement/>
    <AttributeStatement/>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```

laura: Notice the assertion uses a _default_ namespace (no prefix) for assertion elements while the Response uses `samlp:` and the assertion uses no `saml:` prefix. Customer said their IdP started emitting the assertion without the `saml:` prefix after an IdP update.

daniel: Hmm. Our SP metadata parser expects assertion elements either in the `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion` namespace specifically, but it also relied on the `saml:` prefix in previous IdP outputs. If the assertion elements are in the same namespace but lack the prefix, XML namespace resolution should still work. Are we sure the namespace declarations are present on the Assertion element?

laura: They showed `xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"` on the Assertion element (see pasted snippet). So it is declared, just no prefix.

mika: Can you attach a snippet of our ACS log around the failure? The typical recipient mismatch happens if the `Assertion/Subject/SubjectConfirmation/SubjectConfirmationData` `Recipient` attribute doesn’t exactly match the ACS URL in SP metadata (including trailing slash, port, querystring). Also some of our strict checks normalize by prefix presence in the Response; maybe a parser quirk introduced in the cert-rotation deploy.

laura: Log excerpt: ```
[SAML] 2026-04-15T12:35:01Z ERROR validate_saml: recipient mismatch: got="https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs" expected="https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs/"
[SAML] 2026-04-15T12:35:01Z DEBUG parsed_assertion_ns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" prefix_present=false
```

laura: Customer insists their `Recipient` value matches the ACS without trailing slash (we expect trailing slash). They claim nothing changed on their side except IdP cert rotation.

daniel: Two likely causes: (1) IdP rotation process also swapped a metadata template that altered ACS formatting (maybe dropped trailing slash), or (2) our metadata refresh / parser behavior changed in last deploy — I recall a PR that tightened XML namespace handling to mitigate an XEE/namespace attack vector. That PR may have inadvertently required prefix presence for some code paths.

mika: Ops-bot, can you check if we rolled any SAML parsing or auth-related code around that window?

ops-bot: Detected deploy 2026-04-15T11:50:00Z -> release/infra-auth: ran migrations and updated saml-parser v1.3.7 -> v1.4.0. Related commit: github.com/redwood/saml-parser@8f9a.

mika: that lines up. PR notes mention "namespace handling stricter matching". We need to determine if that change rejects default-namespaced assertions when prefix missing. If so, that's a regression.

daniel: Quick repro: wget the customer's metadata and run our local parser. Steps I used:```
curl -s https://idp.customers.example.com/metadata | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'
python3 -c "from redwood_saml import Parser; print(Parser().parse(\"https://idp.customers.example.com/metadata\"))"
```
I got a parse warning about prefixed elements.

mika: Thanks. Two actionable items: (A) Ask customer to confirm their IdP metadata hasn't changed except the cert; provide exact `Recipient` attribute value (B) Rollback or patch our parser to accept default-namespace assertions until we ship a proper fix. Temporary mitigation: add a metadata-mapping rule that normalizes ACS URLs (strip/append trailing slash) in our identity gateway config so recipient check is tolerant.

laura: Jacob (customer) replied in ticket: they have Recipient="https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs" (no trailing slash) and their metadata only changed cert element. They attached their metadata XML.

laura: I diffed their old vs new metadata (they provided both). Only the KeyDescriptor/X509Data changed. Nothing else changed including ACS entries.

daniel: So likely our deploy is the cause. Mika, can you open a hotfix to relax the parser check and push a canary to staging+prod? Also add an immediate shim that will normalize Recipient comparison to be tolerant of trailing slash differences. Create an incident ticket for tracking.

mika: On it. Creating ticket INC-5467 and branch hotfix/saml-default-ns-fix. I'll push the shim to canary in 15m and monitor.

mika: (later) Deployed hotfix to canary, forced metadata refresh for the customer (invalidated cache). I also added a temporary tolerant Recipient comparison: we compare exact match OR match after adding/removing trailing slash.

ops-bot: Metadata refresh for entityID https://idp.customers.example.com/ scheduled, cache invalidation triggered for customer id 3245.

laura: Customer reports they can now login. Jacob: "Thanks, login works again. Not sure why it broke but appreciate the fast patch." :thumbsup:

daniel: We'll keep the hotfix for a few days while we write a proper parser fix and add unit tests for default-namespace assertions. Mika, assign a follow-up PR to revert the shim after proper fix with tests and add a regression test to CI.

mika: Yep. PR created: github.com/redwood/saml-parser/pull/132 - adds namespace handling tests + fixes parser to accept default-namespaced assertion elements. Setting target for scheduled deploy tomorrow.

laura: Closing the support loop with customer. Logging incident notes in #incidents. Thanks all.

jacob_cust: Thanks everyone, appreciate the speedy help!
